originalTitle: IIAS opposes Ujjivan SFB RSU plan over disclosure concerns
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening: a company called Ujjivan Small Finance Bank wants to give some of its employees special rewards called RSUs (Restricted Stock Units). However, a group called IIAS, which helps investors make informed decisions, doesn't think this is a good idea because the bank hasn't clearly explained how these rewards will be given out. The bank says that employees will get these rewards if they meet certain targets, like making more money for the bank, and if they do their jobs well. This matters because it affects how the bank is run and how its money is used, which can impact the people who invest in the bank.

originalTitle: Buffett to offload Berkshire stake in 8 years, Gates snubbed
simplifiedContent: Warren Buffett, a well-known investor, plans to give away all of his shares in Berkshire Hathaway, a company he owns a part of, over the next 8 years. He will be donating these shares to charity, but surprisingly, he won't be giving any to the Gates Foundation, which is run by Bill Gates. Instead, he will be giving the shares to charities run by his own family members. This matters because it shows a change in Buffett's plans for his wealth and his relationship with other wealthy individuals, like Bill Gates. By giving away his shares, Buffett is essentially giving up control of a large part of Berkshire Hathaway.

originalTitle: RBI proposes easing rules for mutual funds, insurers to acquire higher stake in banks
simplifiedContent: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is thinking of making it easier for big investors, like mutual funds and insurance companies, to own a larger share of banks. Currently, these investors need to get special permission every time they want to increase their stake in a bank. The RBI is proposing to allow them to own up to 10% of a bank's shares with just one-time approval, instead of needing repeated permission. This change is intended to make things simpler for these big investors. The RBI is asking for public comments on this idea until August 4, 2026.

originalTitle: Govt reviews fresh bids for IDBI Bank as stake sale process gathers pace
simplifiedContent: The Indian government and LIC (a large insurance company) own a significant portion of IDBI Bank, and they want to sell some of their shares. They plan to sell a total of 60.72% of the bank's shares, which includes 30.48% owned by the government and 30.24% owned by LIC. This sale will also give the buyer control over the bank's management. This matters because it could lead to changes in how the bank is run and potentially impact its performance. The sale is a significant step as the government and LIC currently own almost 95% of the bank.

originalTitle: Alpine Texworld IPO off to a slow start; subscribed 0.28 times on Day 1; GMP indicates modest listing
simplifiedContent: Alpine Texworld's initial public offering (IPO) got off to a slow start, with not many people showing interest in buying its shares on the first day. In fact, the response was so low that the shares were subscribed only 0.28 times, meaning that for every share available, only 0.28 shares were bought. The company is trying to raise ₹126 crore to grow its business and pay off debts, but the slow start may not be a good sign. The response was particularly low from individual investors and non-institutional investors, although big institutional investors showed more interest. This slow start may affect how the company's shares perform when they start trading.

originalTitle: IBM shares plunge 26% after Q2 earnings forecast falls short of estimates
simplifiedContent: IBM's stock price dropped sharply by 26% to $228 because the company's sales for the second quarter were lower than expected, with revenue of $17.2 billion. This happened because customers are spending less money, according to IBM's CEO Arvind Krishna. As a result, the stock had its biggest one-day drop in decades. This also affected other similar companies, which saw losses after IBM's announcement. The significant decline in IBM's stock price is a notable event, with the stock now trading at $228.
